claims.text: A machine-learning-guided, high-throughput combinatorial approach can rapidly identify promising refractory high-entropy alloy compositions.
The identified RHEA compositions can simultaneously exhibit high intrinsic strength, good ductility, and low weight.
The proposed closed-loop strategy combines high-throughput synthesis and characterization with machine-learning prediction and refinement.
Combinatorial sputtering or additive manufacturing with composition gradients can be used to create the alloy library.
Rapid mechanical testing and density measurements can evaluate systematically varied refractory-alloy compositions.
Thermokinetic and phase-stability descriptors can supplement the experimental data used by the model.
Optimized composition influences grain-size distribution, phase formation, and defect density in the RHEA.
Data-driven predictions can navigate the large RHEA compositional space by identifying relationships among composition, processing, and microstructure.
Microstructural features control the trade-offs among strength, ductility, and density.
Feeding iterative experimental results back into the machine-learning model refines its predictions.
The approach will identify RHEA compositions with improved yield strength and ductility while retaining lower density than conventional refractory alloys.
Traditional thermo-kinetic simulation methods are slower and less efficient at exploring the full high-dimensional composition space.
Model validity is limited to refractory alloys within the investigated composition ranges and processing conditions.
Machine-learning predictions may not transfer reliably across different processing conditions.
The model may not accurately capture complex microstructural phenomena governing the strength-ductility balance.
